messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: P1 - runtime.request_queueing.high_latency detected in prod (root: runtime-api). Alert at 23:00 UTC. Trigger: median request latency > 1200ms and queue depth > 200 for 5m.

sanjay: I'm on it. seeing increased 503/504s in the dashboard too. EU regions spiking.

tia: I can start triage. Is there a recent deploy? ops-bot, any deploys in last 30m?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: No deploys to runtime-api in the last 60m.

maria: Runtime metrics look like KV-cache thrash + lots of long-running decoding. max_in_flight is saturated on several nodes.

sanjay: ok, runbook step 1: limit new requests into runtime-pool and trigger shedding for non-critical routes. who can flip the rate limit?

tia: I can apply a temporary rate cap per-org via the edge proxy. Suggest: global soft limit 60rps per org and 20rps for trial-tier. That should reduce pressure.

lucy: Support: we're already seeing ~12 customers with errors and a handful reporting degraded streaming. Notified a customer success lead.

maria: Also recommend disabling realtime streaming on non-enterprise routes until stable. Streaming racks use more memory and keep KV caches hot.

jamal: I'm taking the proxy changes. Applying policy now:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/policies/rate-limit -d '{"scope":"org","limit":60}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

jamal: applied. Ops UI shows org-level limit at 60rps. Leaving canary window 2m.

sanjay: good. tia, can you bump per-node max_in_flight down to 8 (from 16) to favor fairness and reduce head-of-line blocking?

tia: doing it via autoscaler config. Pushing patch:
```yaml
runtime_pools:
  - name: runtime-std
    max_in_flight: 8
    queue_size: 500
```
Patch applied, rolling restart of affected pods.

maria: also setting shedding rule for `embeddings` route: priority=low -> drop when queue>300.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-231555 (runtime backpressure). Severity: P1. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-231555

sanjay: tagging product & CS: @nate @lucy — customer impact approx 12 customers, worst for EU-1. We'll need a public status update.

nate: preparing a short status page. please provide ETA for mitigation.

jamal: early results: overall 95th latency dropped ~40% in 3m after rate limits. 503 rate decreased from 2.8% -> 0.9%. Still some nodes showing queue drain lag.

maria: temp timeout tuning: reduce decode timeout from 45s -> 20s for non-enterprise models to free up in-flight slots. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl set-config runtime.decode_timeout --env prod --value 20s --selector "tier!=enterprise"
```

maria: applied. watch the backlog.

lucy: CS update drafted: "We are experiencing elevated latency and intermittent errors for a subset of customers in EU. Mitigations are in progress (rate limiting, shedding, timeout changes). No data loss. We will update in 30 minutes."

sanjay: good. also disabling a non-critical feature flag (structured-output-preview) that was high-traffic. flipping now.

ops-bot: feature-flag: structured-output-preview -> disabled by sanjay at 23:07 UTC.

jamal: metrics: queue depth trending down, but one rack (eu-west-3) still shows slow drain. I recommend cordoning that rack and migrating traffic away if it doesn't recover in 5m.

tia: cordon command ready: `kubectl label node <node> cordoned=runtime-incident` then evict podset. Do you want me to proceed?

sanjay: go ahead, coordinate eviction to avoid cascading restarts.

tia: cordoned eu-west-3-rack-7 and started controlled evictions.

maria: migrating ~30% of traffic to fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) for trial and free tiers to reduce token cost and CPU pressure. Routing change applied.

jamal: after migration, 95th latency improved further. 503s now 0.3%. good signal.

sanjay: nice work. Next: prepare a short postmortem checklist. Who can own immediate RCA? I nominate maria + tia to pair for root-cause, jamal to own mitigation timeline, nate to own customer comms.

maria: happy to own RCA. initial hypothesis: combination of a sudden traffic burst + a small memory leak in streaming path + aggressive max_in_flight default.

nate: I'll push status update to status.redwood.ai and loop in account leads.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-231555 status -> mitigated (live mitigations stable). Handing to oncall followup.

sanjay: handing over to night on-call jamal for monitoring until 03:00 UTC. @jamal you're oncall handoff.

jamal: got it. I'll monitor the queues and escalate if anything reappears. documented steps in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-backpressure.

lucy: support will follow up with impacted customers and offer logs + incident summary.

sanjay: thanks everyone. quick retro action items: 1) increase default per-node telemetry for queue/backpressure, 2) add automated trigger to reduce max_in_flight when queue>200, 3) run chaos test for streaming memory behavior. Assign owners in postmortem.

maria: I'll start the postmortem draft and include perf graphs.

jamal: leaving detailed mitigation timeline in the incident ticket before I go.

sanjay: closing thread here — monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
